solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Food parcels innocent presented under fire (8)

indicatorNotes.parcels: to parcel is to wrap up, so FEED wraps round the innocent

blocks.note: a lamb is the stock image of innocence

annotation.surface: A charity hands out food parcels to an innocent victim of shelling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Under fire' suggests a war zone; in the kitchen it means set alight with brandy, which is what the definition describes.
annotation.definitionFit: A flambéed dish is served with spirit poured over it and set alight.

entries.clue: Craft pine hoop bound with willow, perhaps (8)

indicatorNotes.bound with: the hoop is tied inside the bat

blocks.note: to pine for something is to long for it
cricket bats are made of willow

annotation.surface: Instructions for a basket-maker weaving a pine hoop into willow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pine' and 'willow' both look like timber for the craft, but pine is the verb and willow stands for a cricket bat.
annotation.definitionFit: A longboat is a large rowing boat, a craft.

entries.clue: Average pug, Spooner’s wee pal? (12)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Rev Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: wee = WIDDLE, which takes the M from the second word
pal = MATE, which takes the W from WIDDLE

annotation.surface: Someone describes their unremarkable pug as the dog's little companion.
annotation.walkthrough: The pug is not a dog but a pugilist, a boxer; 'average' puts him in the middle weight class. A widdle is British slang for a wee.
annotation.definitionFit: A middleweight is a boxer of middling weight, an average pug.

entries.clue: Visor certainly was required to block out all but edges in eclipse (8)

indicatorNotes.to block: the words sit in the way between the two edge letters
indicatorNotes.all but edges: keep only the outside letters of eclipse, discarding everything else

annotation.surface: Advice that a visor was essential for watching the eclipse.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is eye-safety advice for an eclipse, and the answer belongs in that picture.
annotation.definitionFit: An eyeshade is a visor worn to shield the eyes from light.

entries.clue: Reduce diamonds still with 25 per cent off (7)

indicatorNotes.with 25 per cent off: WINDLESS has eight letters; a quarter of them, the last two, go

annotation.surface: A jeweller marks down diamonds that are still for sale at a quarter off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb in a sale notice; it is the adjective for calm air.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the intransitive sense: numbers that reduce over time shrink away.
annotation.definitionNote: dwindle is mostly intransitive (become smaller), and 'reduce' can be too

entries.clue: Resounding effect of vicar dealing with upset bishop (6)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns RE upside down

annotation.surface: A vicar handles a bishop who has been upset, with loud consequences.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' seems to describe the bishop, but it acts on 'dealing with' before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Reverb is an echoing effect added to sound, a resounding effect.

entries.clue: Put strain on island transport (4)

blocks.note: the verb for burdening someone's patience or resources

annotation.surface: Tourists overload an island's transport system.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'strain' and 'transport' as one complaint; the split comes after 'island', and TAX is meant as the verb, not a levy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a cab is one kind of transport.

entries.clue: Forceful macho types check bags (8)

indicatorNotes.bags: to bag is to put inside, so VET holds the macho types

annotation.surface: Aggressive bodybuilders are asked to check their bags.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bags' reads as luggage, but it is the verb that does the containing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a vehement protest is a forceful, passionate one.

entries.clue: Keg a crew possibly salvaged from this? (8)

annotation.definition: Keg a crew possibly salvaged from this?

indicatorNotes.possibly: the letters could possibly be arranged otherwise

annotation.surface: A shipwreck from which a crew might rescue a keg.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the fodder is exactly the kind of thing hauled out of a wreck.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue asks what a crew might rescue a keg from, and the broken remains of a ship are exactly that.

entries.clue: Name religious festival around end of Ramadan (4)

indicatorNotes.end of: take the last letter of Ramadan

annotation.surface: A request to name the festival that comes around when Ramadan ends.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is accurate, since Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan, which makes 'Name' look like an instruction rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a girl's first name, as in Enid Blyton, and setters often use 'name' this loosely.

entries.clue: Criminal invited cops as deterrent (12)

indicatorNotes.Criminal: a criminal version of the word is a corrupted one
indicatorNotes.cops: to cop is to catch, so the anagram catches the next word

annotation.surface: A criminal who calls the police round, as a way of putting others off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cops' looks like the police and is the verb; 'as' is easy to pass over but supplies SINCE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything that puts people off doing something works as a deterrent.

entries.clue: Gutted those Republican donors had to switch allegiance (12)

indicatorNotes.Gutted: gutting removes the insides, leaving T…E

annotation.surface: Disappointed Republican donors who were forced to defect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British for bitterly disappointed, and that is how the surface reads it; here it empties THOSE. 'Had' is ATE, not part of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To tergiversate is to change sides or equivocate.

entries.clue: Wine shop token applied to case of Garnacha (6)

indicatorNotes.case of: the case is the outside, first and last letters

blocks.note: to bode is to be a token or sign of what is coming

annotation.surface: A wine shop voucher used against a case of Garnacha, a Spanish red.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Token' looks like a voucher, but it is the verb meaning portend. 'Case' is both a box of wine and the word's outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing from Spanish, where the word names a wine cellar or wine shop; in American usage it has drifted to a corner store.

entries.clue: Deliver lecture that starts with short story (8)

indicatorNotes.short: cut the last letter off LIE

blocks.note: a story is a LIE, shortened
to lecture someone is to berate them

annotation.surface: A speaker is told to open the lecture with a short story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' pairs with 'lecture' as public speaking; it means set free.
annotation.definitionFit: The biblical sense of deliver, as in 'deliver us from evil': to set free.

entries.clue: Lose one’s rag when Tesla cuts in under driver’s control (7)

indicatorNotes.cuts in: the T cuts into the phrase

blocks.note: to lose one's rag (temper) is to SEE RED
T is the symbol for the tesla, a unit of magnetism

annotation.surface: A driver loses their temper when a Tesla cuts in front of them.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tesla looks like the car doing the cutting in; it is the SI unit, T.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive phrase for the past participle: a car being guided by the wheel is in the driver's hands.
annotation.definitionNote: the definition is an adjectival phrase; STEERED is the past participle

entries.clue: Mass of seaweed fool brought aboard small Greek ship (8)

indicatorNotes.brought aboard: the fool is put inside the ship

annotation.surface: A tangle of seaweed and a fool taken on board a small Greek boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The Argo, Jason's ship in the Golden Fleece myth, is the crossword's usual Greek ship.
annotation.definitionFit: Sargasso is gulfweed, the floating seaweed that gives the Sargasso Sea its name.

entries.clue: Post’s more expensive, isn’t it? (7)

annotation.surface: A grumble that postage has gone up again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Post' reads as mail, and the clue is written to sound like a complaint about stamp prices; it is a vertical pole.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from building and sport: the vertical members of a frame or goal are its uprights.

entries.clue: Expert players given favourable draw you’d say profit (8)

indicatorNotes.you’d say: what you would say out loud, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: pros who are seeded in a tournament draw

annotation.surface: Top players with a kind draw are said to cash in.
annotation.walkthrough: In a tennis draw, seeded players are kept apart so they meet late, which is the favourable draw.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from business: the proceeds of a sale are the money it brings in.

entries.clue: Present repeats on the radio for positive response from listeners (4,4)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: broadcast sound, so heard not seen

annotation.surface: A radio station airs repeats, and listeners approve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repeats' looks like reruns on air; it tells you to say HERE twice. The definition fits well, as the phrase is a cry of agreement from an audience.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Hear, hear!' is what an audience calls out to agree.

entries.clue: Ireland’s border guards admired bottle (7)

indicatorNotes.guards: the border protects what is inside it

blocks.note: a hem is a border on cloth

annotation.surface: Guards on the Irish border praised for their courage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Border guards' reads as one phrase, but it splits: the border does the guarding. Bottle is British slang for nerve.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: bottle is nerve, and nerve that earns admiration is the heroic kind.

entries.clue: Sound clearly dies out in the front rows (8)

indicatorNotes.out: out as in out of place or out of joint: the letters are no longer where they belong

annotation.surface: A noise is heard clearly, then fades in the front rows of a theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dies out' reads as fading; 'out' is the rearranging word.
annotation.definitionFit: Ringside seats are the front rows at a boxing match.

entries.clue: Legion is expecting flanks to charge (6)

indicatorNotes.flanks: the answer sits between the outside parts of these words

annotation.surface: A legion waits for its flanks to charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charge' reads as a cavalry attack; it means give an electric charge.
annotation.definitionFit: The physics sense of charge: adding or stripping electrons leaves an atom electrically charged.

entries.clue: Unrequited love just discovered, alas (3-3)

blocks.note: love = nil = O, as in tennis
ay, an old cry of woe

annotation.surface: Someone learns, too late, that their love is not returned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Love' belongs in the surface's heartbreak, and here it is just O.
annotation.definitionFit: One-way love goes in one direction only, unrequited.

entries.clue: American forces on US vessel filmed spy (6,6)

indicatorNotes.on: one thing placed on another comes after it in an across answer, so POWERS goes second

blocks.note: US + TIN, a tin being a vessel

annotation.surface: American forces aboard a US warship catch a spy on camera.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' reads as a ship; it is a tin can. Austin Powers is Mike Myers's spoof spy of the 1990s films.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a spy known from the screen, the spoof agent of three comedy films.

entries.clue: Blazer king lost (4)

annotation.surface: A king has lost his jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blazer' reads as a jacket; it is anything that blazes.
annotation.definitionFit: Sunk means ruined, lost, as in 'we're sunk'.

entries.clue: Cautionary rating in the main reflected graphic references (4)

indicatorNotes.in: a rating in something sits inside it, so X is placed within the sea
indicatorNotes.reflected: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so SEA reads AES

blocks.note: the main = the sea, turned round
X was the old British film certificate for adults only

annotation.surface: Warnings in a nautical chart's references.
annotation.walkthrough: The main is the poetic term for the sea. 'Graphic' means of graphs here: the axes are what you read values against.
annotation.definitionFit: Axes are the reference lines on a graph.

entries.clue: Outline of little horse facing left is on front of sketchbook (8)

indicatorNotes.facing left: in an across clue, pointing leftwards means read backwards

blocks.note: PONY'S, belonging to the little horse, turned round
as it stands, placed on (after) the S

annotation.surface: An artist's sketchbook opens with the outline of a pony facing left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outline' fits the sketch so well that it hides as the definition, a summary.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the brief summary of a plot or argument is its outline.

entries.clue: Old men with guns heading for Maine and wild turkeys (8)

annotation.surface: Old men with guns head off to Maine to shoot wild turkeys.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a hunting trip; the definition reads the musket-armed soldiers of old as a body of troops.
annotation.definitionFit: Musketry can mean musketeers collectively, old soldiers with guns.
